## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Top call Aurora kinase inhibitors is justified over runner-ups. At 0.3, 1.0, and 3.0 µM, frac_large_nucleus is z=+80.7, +70.3, and +101.4 with increased integrated DNA, yet tubulin profiles are near-normal and frac_mitotic_like is depressed; this pattern argues against Eg5 or microtubule stabilizer/destabilizer arrest. Probability 0.88 is reasonably calibrated given the large, dose-consistent phenotype; no additional affordable step is needed.

## Unblinding

Compound: **AZ258** (PubChem CID [59396138](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/59396138))

Identity check: from the BBBC021 structure (the name is not in PubChem)

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: agent said **Aurora kinase inhibitors**, BBBC021 annotates **Aurora kinase inhibitors**.

## Reflection

The Aurora call was driven by extreme large-nucleus signals at 0.3, 1.0 and 3.0 uM with frac_large_nucleus z=+80.7, +70.3 and +101.4 and nuc_area z=+42.6 to +44.9, plus intact tubulin profiles and depressed mitotic-like fraction at those doses, and 9/10 Aurora neighbors on compare_to_reference_atlas. This matches reported Aurora B inhibition inducing mitotic defect and polyploidy (PMID 35051862).

What could have misled was the high-dose well at 30 uM with tub_glcm_contrast z=+28.9, act_glcm_contrast z=+22.6 and tub_std z=+15.9, and the microscopist call of Microtubule stabilizers on that field, plus 3-point dose_response trends with Spearman rho=-1.00 for frac_large_nucleus and nuc_area and rho=+1.00 for tub_mean.

I kept Aurora at 0.88 because the massive polyploidy was dose-consistent across 0.3-3 uM with near-normal tubulin, the tubulin texture spike was confined to 30 uM where large-nucleus signal falls, and the atlas and visual failed-cytokinesis pattern argued against Eg5 or microtubule arrest; the limitation was relying on only 3-4 wells without replicates or phospho-H3/DNA-content confirmation.

What was right:
- Prioritized massive frac_large_nucleus and nuc_area enlargement at 0.3-3 uM (e3, e7, e13) as failed cytokinesis/polyploidy rather than generic cytotoxicity
- Used compare_to_reference_atlas 9/10 Aurora neighbors (e5) plus depressed frac_mitotic_like to reject Eg5 and microtubule stabilizer/destabilizer arrest
- Correctly interpreted 30 uM tubulin texture spike (e2) as secondary high-dose toxicity because primary polyploidy persisted with normal tubulin at 0.3-3 uM

What was wrong or missed:
- High-dose acquire_well at 30 uM (e2) and describe_phenotype at high dose (e8) transiently supported Microtubule stabilizers and inflated that alternative to 0.03
- 3-well dose_response trends (e9, e10 rho=-1.00; e11 rho=+1.00) were over-interpreted as trends despite n=3 and absolute z-scores remaining huge, reflecting fall-off at toxic high dose rather than lack of dose dependence
- Did not acquire low-dose or replicate wells to define polyploidy onset/EC50 and did not obtain phospho-H3 or DNA-content data during the blinded run, leaving mechanism inferred from morphology plus atlas alone

Proposed next experiment: Phospho-Histone H3 Ser10 immunofluorescence plus DNA-content flow cytometry at 0.3-3 uM to confirm loss of Aurora activity and quantify polyploidy/endoreduplication versus mitotic arrest.

- PMID [35051862](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35051862/): The phytochemical, corynoline, diminishes Aurora kinase B activity to induce mitotic defect and polyploidy. *Biomed Pharmacother* (2022) — Inhibition of Aurora kinase B activity induces mitotic defects and polyploidy.
- PMID [22242557](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22242557/): Danusertib, an aurora kinase inhibitor. *Expert Opin Investig Drugs* (2012) — Danusertib is a characterized Aurora kinase inhibitor.
